bibliography.abstract: Urbanization alters land surface characteristics and intensifies Surface Urban Heat Island (SUHI) conditions, particularly in rapidly growing urban areas. However, municipality level studies in Kerala linking Land Use Land Cover (LULC) change, Land Surface Temperature (LST), spectral indices, and urban planning remain limited. This study examines the spatiotemporal dynamics of LULC change and SUHI intensification in Palakkad Municipality to support sustainable urban planning. Multi-temporal satellite datasets were analyzed using multiyear average data for four assessment periods (1990–2000, 2001–2010, 2011–2020, and 2021–2025), using Landsat 5 TM, Landsat 7 ETM+, Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS, and PlanetScope imagery. Supervised Support Vector Machine classification was used to map five LULC classes, while NDVI, NDBI, NDMI, LST, SUHI, and UTFVI were derived to characterize vegetation, built-up conditions, moisture, and surface thermal conditions. The LULC classification achieved overall accuracies ranging from 82.39% to 99.35%, with Kappa coefficients ranging from 0.7611 to 0.9911. The results show substantial urban expansion during the study period. Built-up area increased from 26.94% in 1990 to 77.13% in 2025, while agricultural land declined from 36.36% to 3.78%. Mixed vegetation, open land, and waterbodies also showed declining or fragmented patterns. Mean LST increased from 37.76 °C during 1990–2000 to 38.52 °C during 2021—2025, indicating gradual urban surface warming. Higher temperatures were concentrated in dense built-up areas and transport corridors, whereas vegetated and moisture rich areas recorded lower thermal stress. UTFVI analysis confirmed deterioration in thermal ecological conditions, with the worst thermal stress zones expanding in recent years. The study concludes that conversion of agricultural and vegetated land into impervious built-up surfaces is a major driver of SUHI intensification. The findings recommend conserving vegetation, agricultural land, open spaces, and water bodies, along with green corridors, cool roofs, permeable pavements, and GIS based heat risk planning for sustainable urban development.
bibliography.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of land use/land cover change and surface urban heat island intensification for sustainable urban planning in palakkad municipality, Kerala, India

en.what: Using Landsat and PlanetScope satellite imagery covering 1990 to 2025 across four time intervals, the authors tracked land surface changes and urban heat island intensification in Palakkad Municipality, India using Support Vector Machine classification (accuracies between 82.39% and 99.35%). Built-up surfaces expanded from 26.94% to 77.13% of the municipality while agricultural coverage fell from 36.36% to 3.78%. Consequently, average land surface temperature rose from 37.76 °C to 38.52 °C, with maximum thermal stress shifting toward transit networks and dense commercial zones.
en.why: The findings convert land loss into quantified thermal degradation for a rapidly growing Indian municipality, replacing qualitative assumptions about local urban heat with long-term spatial temperature trajectories.
